summary:
Project Kagami is a web tool that reflects any point on the Moon or Mars back onto Earth.

The user picks a destination, chooses what matters most (geology, terrain, thermal extremes, water ice, atmosphere, radiation, landing and rover mobility, or best overall), and clicks a point on the surface map. Project Kagami analyzes the terrain at that location using NASA mission data and returns the top 3 Earth locations that most closely match it, with match percentages, a map, comparison charts, and a detailed metrics table.

This helps researchers and mission planners find realistic places on Earth to test equipment, train crews, and rehearse operations for permanent lunar bases and Mars missions.
details:
Our project is an interactive planetary terrain analysis platform that identifies Earth locations with geological and environmental characteristics similar to selected locations on the Moon and Mars. Users select a planetary body, choose a comparison priority, and click a location on the map. The backend analyzes its terrain, geology, mineralogy, temperature, water-ice potential, atmospheric conditions, and mobility factors, then ranks the three closest Earth analogs with similarity percentages and visual comparisons.

We have used React + JavaScript + Tailwind CSS + HTML to make the front end. Python with scikit-learn, pandas and numpy was used to create the location matching algorithm, with FastAPI to connect the backend to the frontend and SQLLite for the database.

The creative part of our project is that, unlike competitors which are only considering data from known permanent bases on the moon/mars, our project allows the user to find analagous sites for any location on the moon/mars. This can be beneficial to future mission planners, engineers and researchers to pick analogous sites for new landing locations.

Our team considered all relevant data found in our research.
